akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿أَن تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ﴾, i.e. for fear that your deeds become void. It may be said: "اسْمُكِ الحائِطَ أَنْ يَمِيلَ" (… the wall lest it lean). «[Translator's note: so in the text («اسمك»); presumably «أَمْسِكِ الحائطَ», "hold the wall".]»

akhfash:13-13.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ﴾ with kasra because it is a fresh start, and he did not construe it on ﴿لِتَعَارَفُوۤاْ﴾.

daas-irab:12-13.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيراً﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿مِنَ الظَّنِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كثيرا. ﴿إِنَّ بَعْضَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿الظَّنِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿إِثْمٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿وَلا تَجَسَّسُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا يَغْتَبْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by the lā of prohibition. ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿بَعْضاً﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَيُحِبُّ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation and rebuke, and a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb. ﴿أَحَدُكُمْ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, and its mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَخِيهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ. ﴿مَيْتاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and a past verb with its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is for lengthening (ishbāʿ); the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ a particle of resumption, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its two predicates; the nominal clause is an explanation of cause and has no grammatical position. ﴿يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ the i'rab of its like has preceded. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿خَلَقْناكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿مِنْ ذَكَرٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَأُنْثى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ذكر; the nominal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَجَعَلْناكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿شُعُوباً﴾ its second mafʿūl. ﴿وَقَبائِلَ﴾ conjoined to شعوبا. ﴿لِتَعارَفُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an concealed after the lām of causation, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعلناكم. ﴿إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَتْقاكُمْ﴾ the khabar of inna; the nominal clause is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its two predicates; the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:14-15.t: ﴿قالَتِ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الْأَعْرابُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿قُولُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَسْلَمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and an imperfect verb, jussive by lammā. ﴿الْإِيمانُ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and in is conditional, governing the jussive. ﴿تُطِيعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause تطيعوا is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿لا يَلِتْكُمْ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the kāf is its mafʿūl and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ أَعْمالِكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its two predicates; the clause is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl) and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa). ﴿الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَمْ يَرْتابُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَجاهَدُوا﴾ conjoined to آمنوا. ﴿بِأَمْوالِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ conjoined to أموالهم. ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الصَّادِقُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-18.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَتُعَلِّمُونَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of rebuking interrogation, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِدِينِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ the two are attached to عليم. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَمُنُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative. ﴿أَسْلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا تَمُنُّوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيَّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿إِسْلامَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿بَلِ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَمُنُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to يمن. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative. ﴿هَداكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl; the fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِلْإِيمانِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition. ﴿أَنْ﴾ conditional, governing the jussive. [Translator's note: the source writes «أن» here; the Quranic word is ﴿إِنْ﴾ (in), the conditional particle.] ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ its khabar; the verbal clause is initial and has no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because what precedes indicates it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿غَيْبَ﴾ its mafʿūl. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), and hā is for drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) of ayyuhā. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the vocative clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لا تُقَدِّمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿يَدَيِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined to what came before. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (اللَّهِ); as mafʿūl bihi it is اللَّهَ.] ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its two khabars (predicates); the clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl). ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا﴾ its i'rab is like the preceding one. ﴿أَصْواتَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَوْقَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿صَوْتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿النَّبِيِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lā is prohibitive. ﴿تَجْهَرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿بِالْقَوْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb. ﴿كَجَهْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿بَعْضِكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِبَعْضٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to jahr. ﴿أَنْ تَحْبَطَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an. ﴿أَعْمالُكُمْ﴾ fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by annexation to an omitted mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يَغُضُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَصْواتَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿رَسُولِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause inna is resumptive. ﴿امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil. ﴿قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لِلتَّقْوى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila of alladhīna. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿مَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَأَجْرٌ﴾ conjoined to maghfira. ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يُنادُونَكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the kāf a mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ وَراءِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْحُجُراتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause inna is resumptive.

daas-irab:5-7.t: ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and law is a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿صَبَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive. ﴿تَخْرُجَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after ḥattā. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ṣabarū. ﴿لَكانَ﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of law. ﴿كان﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿خَيْراً﴾ its khabar, and the noun of kāna is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khayran; the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its two khabars; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿جاءَكُمْ﴾ a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فاسِقٌ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِنَبَإٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فَتَبَيَّنُوا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿أَنْ تُصِيبُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿قَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by annexation to an omitted mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the implied form being "out of dislike of your striking" (karāhata iṣābatikum). ﴿بِجَهالَةٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَتُصْبِحُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a defective imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its noun. ﴿عَلى ما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to nādimīn. ﴿فَعَلْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā. ﴿نادِمِينَ﴾ khabar, accusative by the yāʾ. ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿فِيكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿رَسُولَ﴾ the postponed noun of anna. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the interpreted maṣdar from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of iʿlamū. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿يُطِيعُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِي كَثِيرٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنَ الْأَمْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to kathīr. ﴿لَعَنِتُّمْ﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَلكِنَّ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lākinna is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its noun. [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (اللَّهِ); as the noun of lākinna it is اللَّهَ.] ﴿حَبَّبَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar of lākinna. ﴿إِلَيْكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْإِيمانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَزَيَّنَهُ﴾ conjoined to ḥabbaba. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَكَرَّهَ﴾ conjoined to zayyana. ﴿إِلَيْكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْكُفْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالْفُسُوقَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَالْعِصْيانَ﴾ conjoined to what came before. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الرَّاشِدُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:8-10.t: ﴿فَضْلًا﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) faḍlan. ﴿وَنِعْمَةً﴾ conjoined to faḍlan. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ two khabars (predicates); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and in is conditional. ﴿طائِفَتانِ﴾ the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the alif. ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of ṭāʾifatān. ﴿اقْتَتَلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the omitted protasis clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَأَصْلِحُوا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿فَإِنْ بَغَتْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, in is conditional, and a past verb. ﴿إِحْداهُما﴾ fāʿil. ﴿عَلَى الْأُخْرى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is initial. ﴿فَقاتِلُوا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿تَبْغِي﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿حَتَّى تَفِيءَ﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive, and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after ḥattā, its fāʿil latent. ﴿إِلى أَمْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to qātilū. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ a conjunction, and in is a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿فاءَتْ﴾ a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَأَصْلِحُوا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis, and an imperative verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿بِالْعَدْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَأَقْسِطُوا﴾ conjoined to aṣliḥū. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl). ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَأَصْلِحُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿أَخَوَيْكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ; the clause is the apodosis of a condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its object. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun. ﴿تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of laʿalla, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿لا يَسْخَرْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā. ﴿قَوْمٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿مِنْ قَوْمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿عَسى﴾ a complete (tāmm) past verb. ﴿أَنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْراً﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an; the wāw is its noun and khayran its khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khayran; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it is the fāʿil of ʿasā. ﴿وَلا نِساءٌ مِنْ نِساءٍ عَسى أَنْ يَكُنَّ خَيْراً مِنْهُنَّ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it, and the clause ʿasā is resumptive. ﴿وَلا تَلْمِزُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive lā; the wāw is its fāʿil and anfusakum its object. ﴿وَلا تَنابَزُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِالْأَلْقابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ﴾ an invariable (jāmid) past verb of blame (dhamm), and its fāʿil. ﴿الْفُسُوقُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause biʾsa is its khabar. ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿الْإِيمانِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and man is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لَمْ يَتُبْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), with its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar, and the clause man is resumptive.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تُقَدِّمُواْ﴾.
The readers agreed on it; and had a reader read (لا تَقْدَموا), it would have been correct. One says: "I went forward (qadamtu) in such-and-such" and "I went ahead (taqaddamtu)".

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لاَ تَرْفَعُوۤاْ أَصْوَاتَكُمْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "بأصواتكم". Like it in speech: "He spoke fine speech" and "He spoke with fine speech".
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَجْهَرُواْ لَهُ بِٱلْقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ.﴾: he says: do not say "O Muḥammad", but say: "O Prophet of Allah, O Messenger of Allah, O Abū al-Qāsim".
His saying: ﴿أَن تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ﴾.
Its meaning is: lest (لا) [your deeds] come to naught; and in it the jussive and the nominative [are possible] if you put (لا) in place of (أن); and it has been explained in more than one place. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: فتحبطَ أعمالكم, and that is evidence for the permissibility of the jussive in it.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱمْتَحَنَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾.
He purified them for piety, as gold is tested with fire, so its good part comes out and its dross falls away.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿مِن وَرَآءِ ٱلْحُجُرَاتِ﴾.
The [usual] way of speech is to give the ḥāʾ and the jīm ḍamma; and some of the Arabs say: الْحُجَرات and الرُّكَبات, and every plural that is said, for three to ten, as ghuraf and ḥujar: when you pluralize it with tāʾ, you give its second [letter] fatḥa. But the ḍamma [180/b] is better than that.
His saying: ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
The delegation of the Banū Tamīm came to him at midday while he, Allah bless him, was asleep, and they began calling: "O Muḥammad, come out to us!" He woke and came out, and there was revealed: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنَادُونَكَ مِن وَرَآءِ ٱلْحُجُرَاتِ﴾ to the end of the verse. After that he gave them leave; their poet and the poet of the Muslims stood up, and an orator of theirs and the orator of the Muslims, and their voices rose in boasting. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down concerning it: ﴿لاَ تَرْفَعُوۤاْ أَصْوَاتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ ٱلنَّبِيِّ﴾.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِن جَآءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتثَبّتُوا﴾.
[This is] the reading of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, and I saw it in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh with thāʾ; and the reading of the people is (فَتَبَيَّنُوا), and their meanings are close, because His saying (فَتَبَيَّنُوا) means: wait until you know, and that is the meaning of تثبتوا. That was only because the Prophet, Allah bless him, sent an agent to the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq to take their alms. When he headed towards them, they came out to meet him to honour him, and he thought they intended to fight him. So he returned to the Prophet, Allah bless him, and said: "They fought me and refused me payment of what they owe." While they were in that state, and the Prophet, Allah bless him, had become angry, the delegation of the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq came to him and said: "We wanted to honour the envoy of the Messenger of Allah and to pay the due to him." The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him, suspected them and did not believe them; so Allah sent down: "ياأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ إِن جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَثَبّتُوا" to the end of the verse, and the verse after it.

farraa:9-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱقْتَتَلُواْ﴾.
He did not say اقتتلتا (dual). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: فخذوا بينهم, in place of فأصلحوا بينهم; and in his reading: حتى يَفِيئُوا إلى أمر الله فإن فاءوا فخذوا بينهم.
His saying: ﴿فَأَصْلِحُواْ بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ﴾.
He did not say بين إخوتكم or إخوانكم; and had that been said, it would have been correct.
It was revealed concerning the clan of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and the clan of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa al-Anṣārī. The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him, passed on a donkey and stopped by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy in the gathering of his people. The donkey of the Messenger of Allah dropped dung, and ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Ubayy] put his hand over his nose and said: "Keep your donkey away; it has annoyed me." Ibn Rawāḥa said to him: "Do you say this of the donkey of the Messenger of Allah? By Allah, it is of better repute than you and your father." The people of this one and the people of that one grew angry, until they fought with hands and sandals; so this verse was revealed.
His saying: ﴿فَقَاتِلُواْ ٱلَّتِي تَبْغِي﴾: the one that does not accept reconciliation. And the Prophet, Allah bless him, reconciled them.

farraa:11-13.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ﴾.
It was revealed because Thābit ibn Qays al-Anṣārī was hard of hearing, and he used to draw near the Prophet, Allah bless him, to hear his speech. He came after one rakʿa of the dawn prayer had been completed, when the people had taken their places near the Messenger of Allah. He began stepping over [them] and saying: "Make room," until he reached a man just short of the Prophet, Allah bless him, and said: "Make room." The man said to him: "You have found a place, so sit." When it became light, he said: "Who is the man?" He said: "So-and-so son of so-and-so." He said: "You are the son of such-and-such a woman", [naming] a mother of his for whom he used to be reproached. That grieved the man, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿لاَ يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ عَسَىٰ أَن يَكُونُواْ خَيْراً مِّنْهُمْ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, as far as I know, it is: عَسَوا أن يكونوا خيراً منهم ولا نساء من نساء عسَين أن يكنَّ خيراً منهن.
And there was also revealed concerning this story: [181/a] ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوباً﴾. The shuʿūb (peoples) are larger than the tribes, and the tribes are larger than the clans (afkhādh). ﴿لِتَعَارَفُوۤاْ﴾: that you may know one another in lineage. ﴿إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ﴾ has kasra; the verb تعارف does not fall on it; and it is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: لتعارفوا بينكم وخيركم عند الله أتقاكم. Thābit said: "By Allah, I will never vie with any man in his lineage again."
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَلْمِزُوۤاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ﴾.
Let not some of you find fault with others; "and do not insult one another with nicknames": a man would say to a man of the Jews who had embraced Islam: "O Jew!", so they were forbidden that; and He said concerning it: ﴿بِئْسَ ٱلاسْمُ ٱلْفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ ٱلإَيمَانِ﴾. And whoever gives fatḥa: أن أكرمكم, it is as though he said: "that you may know one another [in] that the noble one is the pious". Had it been so, it would have been لتعرفوا أن أكرمكم; but لتعارفوا is allowed [in the sense]: that some of you may make known to others that the noblest of you with Allah is the most pious of you.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَجَسَّسُواْ﴾.
The readers are agreed on the jīm. It was revealed specifically about Salmān; they had spoken ill of him.
His saying: ﴿فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ﴾.
The Prophet, Allah bless him, said to them: "Would any of you eat the flesh of his brother after his death?" They said: "No!" He said: "Backbiting is eating his flesh." It is that you say what is in him; and when you say what is not in him, that is slander (al-baht), not backbiting. "So you would hate it", i.e. you have hated it, so do not do it.
And whoever reads فكُرِّهتموه says: it has been made hateful to you; and the meaning, and Allah knows best, is one; and it is in the position of your saying: "The man died (māta)" and "was caused to die (umīta)".

farraa:14-17.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالَتِ ٱلأَعْرَابُ آمَنَّا قُل لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُواْ وَلَـٰكِن قُولُوۤاْ أَسْلَمْنَا﴾.
This was revealed concerning the Bedouins of the Banū Asad. They came to the Prophet, Allah bless him and grant him peace, at Medina with their families, desiring alms, and they kept coming in the evening and the morning, saying: "Give to us, for we have come to you with families and baggage, while the Arabs came to you on the backs of their mounts." So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down: ﴿يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُواْ﴾. (أن) is in the position of the accusative, because in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: يمنون عليك إسلامهم. And had you made it: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْك لأنْ أَسْلَمُوا ("because they submitted"), then when you drop the lām it is an accusative different from the first accusative.
His saying: ﴿أَنْ هَداكُمْ﴾; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: إذ هداكم.
So (أن) is in the position of the accusative, not by the verb falling on it but by the dropping of the preposition (al-ṣifa).
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَلِتْكُمْ﴾.
He will not diminish you, nor wrong you in anything of your deeds. It is from lāta, yalītu, and the readers are agreed on it. Some read: لا يَأْلِتْكم, but I do not like it, because it was written in the codices without alif, and this is not a position where dropping the hamza is allowed. Do you not see His saying (يأتون), (يأمرون) and (يأكلون): the alif was not dropped in any of them, because it is vowelless; the hamza is dropped only when what precedes it is vowelless, but when it itself, meaning the hamza, is vowelless, it remains and is not dropped. He ventured to read it "يألتكم" only because he found ﴿وَمَا أَلَتْنَاهُمْ مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ in one place, and took this from that. The Qurʾān brings both differing dialects. Do you not see His saying: ﴿تُمْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ﴾, while in another place it is: ﴿فَلْيَكْتُبْ وَلْيُمْلِل﴾, and one was not made to conform to the other so that they agree? Lāta yalītu and alata yaʾlitu are two dialects. [He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm ibn Ibrāhīm al-Simmarī narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us.]

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt
﷽
﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ﴾: it has also been read "لا تَقَدَّمُوا", with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the dāl. The meaning is: "when you are commanded to do something, do not do it before the time at which you were commanded to do it." It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that a man slaughtered on the Day of Sacrifice before the prayer of the Sacrifice, and so went ahead before the time; and Allah made known that that is not permissible. In this there is proof that it is not permissible to perform an obligatory act before its time, nor a voluntary act before its time, among those which the Sunna has brought. In this there is also proof that paying zakāt early, before its time, ought not to be permissible. As for what is related, «that the Prophet ﷺ took some of the zakāt in advance from al-ʿAbbās», I do not know of anyone among those who permitted paying zakāt early who argued with anything except this ḥadīth. This, if it is sound, is of two kinds: one of them is that it is a special case; the other is that the need had become severe, so that there was necessity to take the zakāt in advance. The consensus is that giving it at its time is what is right, and it is what is better, if Allah wills. Whoever reads "لا تَقَدَّمُوا", its meaning is like the meaning of ﴿لا تُقَدِّمُوا﴾.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكم فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded them to revere His Prophet, upon him be peace, to lower their voices, to address him with calm and dignity, and to give him precedence in address — that being what they used to do in honouring their chiefs and their great men. The meaning of ﴿كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ﴾ is: do not put him in the position that you hold with one another, so that you say: "يا مُحَمَّدُ" (O Muḥammad); address him by his prophethood, with calm and reverence.
His saying: ﴿أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكُمْ﴾: its meaning is: "do not do that, lest your deeds come to nothing", and the meaning is: "so that your deeds do not come to nothing". So the meaning is the meaning of the lām in "أنْ", and this lām is the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra), like the lām in His saying: ﴿فالتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهم عَدُوًّا وحَزَنًا﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8], the meaning being: "the family of Pharaoh picked him up, so that their affair came to that" — not that they intended it to come to that; but it was in what had been decreed in Allah's prior knowledge that the cause of that outcome was their picking him up. Likewise: "do not raise your voices, lest that become a cause for your deeds coming to nothing". ﴿وَأنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾: this is a notification that the affair of the Prophet ﷺ ought to be exalted and honoured with the utmost honour, and that something may be done regarding the Prophet ﷺ without one being aware of it, and that becomes ruinous for the one who does it or says it. For that reason some of the jurists said: whoever says: "إنَّ زِرَّ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ وسِخٌ" (the button of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is dirty), intending to belittle him, must be killed. This is the doctrine of Mālik and his followers.

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهم عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهم لِلتَّقْوى﴾: He made their hearts pure; and "هُمْ" comes out according to the explanation of the true sense of the language. [Translator's note: the source reads «و”هُمْ“»; «وهو» ("and it") may be intended.] The meaning is: Allah tested their hearts and found them sincere, as you say: "قَدِ امْتَحَنْتُ هَذا الذَّهَبَ، وهَذِهِ الفِضَّةَ" (I have tested this gold and this silver); its interpretation is: I have tried them by melting them until I purified the gold and the silver, and so I knew the true nature of each of them.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِن وراءِ الحُجُراتِ﴾: it is read with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and the jīm, and "اَلْحُجَراتِ" with fatḥa on the jīm. "اَلْحُجْراتِ", with sukūn on the jīm, is permissible in the language, but I do not know anyone who read it with sukūn. We have explained this plural earlier in the book. The singular of al-ḥujurāt is "حُجْرَةٌ" (chamber). It is possible that "اَلْحُجُراتُ" is the plural of "حُجَرٌ", [as in] "حُجُراتٌ"; but the better view is that "اَلْحُجُراتُ" is the plural of "حُجْرَةٌ", and that the fatḥa was allowed as a substitute for the ḍamma because of the heaviness of two ḍammas. These were people of Banū Tamīm who came to the Prophet ﷺ and called to him from behind the chambers. There is a lengthy account about them in the tafsīr (exegesis); its gist is that they came to vie in boasting with the Prophet, and that they did not meet him in the manner due to him, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:5-5.t: He said: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّهم صَبَرُوا حَتّى تَخْرُجَ إلَيْهِمْ لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهم واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, that is: whoever repents after this deed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنْ جاءَكم فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا﴾ — and it is read: "فَتَثَبَّتُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا" (then make sure, lest you harm) — ﴿قَوْمًا بِجَهالَةٍ﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that it was revealed on account of al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba. «The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent him as a collector to gather the alms of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, and between him and them there was iḥna, that is: enmity. When news of him reached them, as he had set out toward them, they said to one another: You know what is between us and this man, so withhold your alms from him. That reached him, and he returned to the Prophet ﷺ and told him that they had withheld the alms from him, that they had apostatised, and that they had prepared weapons for war. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched Khālid ibn al-Walīd with an army, and instructed him to descend on their territory by night: if he saw what indicated their persisting in Islam — the call to prayer, prayer and night vigil — he should refrain from fighting them and ask them for their alms. When Khālid reached them by night, he heard the call to prayer and saw them praying and keeping vigil, and they said to him: We had thought the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding the alms slow in coming; and they handed them over to him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿إنْ جاءَكم فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ﴾», that is: with a report, ﴿فَتَبَيَّنُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهالَةٍ﴾, that is: out of aversion to harming a people in ignorance. This is proof that it is not permissible to accept a report from a fāsiq (a person of evident sinfulness), even if he makes it clear, and that it is permissible to accept the report of a trustworthy person (thiqa). "اَلثِّقَةُ" is one against whom false testimony has not been established, who is not known for sinfulness, and who has not been flogged in a ḥadd punishment, and who in addition has sound discernment.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ فِيكم رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ يُطِيعُكم في كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الأمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ﴾, that is: had he obeyed the like of this informant, who told him what had no basis, you would have fallen into ʿanat; "اَلْعَنَتُ" is corruption and ruin. ﴿وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إلَيْكُمُ الإيمانَ﴾: by this the sincere believers are meant. ﴿وَزَيَّنَهُ في قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾: "فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ" admits two aspects. One of them is that He guided them to it by decisive, clear proofs and the miraculous signs which the Prophet ﷺ brought; the second is that He made it seem fair in their hearts by granting them success (tawfīq).
﴿وَكَرَّهَ إلَيْكُمُ الكُفْرَ والفُسُوقَ والعِصْيانَ﴾: that too is His making clear to them what is against them in disbelief, and His granting them success if they avoid it.
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الرّاشِدُونَ﴾, that is: these whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has granted success by making faith beloved to them and disbelief hateful — those are the rightly guided.

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿فَضْلا مِنَ اللَّهِ ونِعْمَةً﴾ is accusative (manṣūb), a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The meaning is: "Allah did that for you as a bounty from Allah and a favour", that is: for the sake of bounty and favour. Were it outside the Qur'an, "فَضْلٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ ونِعْمَةٌ" (nominative) would be permissible, the meaning being: "that is a bounty from Allah and a favour".

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنْ طائِفَتانِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما فَإنْ بَغَتْ إحْداهُما عَلى الأُخْرى فَقاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي﴾: the transgressing party is the one that deviates from the truth and from what the leaders of the Muslims and their community are upon. ﴿حَتّى تَفِيءَ إلى أمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾: until it returns to the command of Allah. ﴿فَإنْ فاءَتْ﴾: then if it returns, ﴿فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما بِالعَدْلِ وأقْسِطُوا﴾, that is: and be just; ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ المُقْسِطِينَ﴾. It was said that this was revealed on account of two groups of the Anṣār between whom there was fighting, and that was not with swords or weapons; it has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that there was fighting between them with hands and sandals, and throwing of stones at one another.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ إخْوَةٌ فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أخَوَيْكُمْ﴾: it is also read "بَيْنَ إخْوانِكُمْ", "بَيْنَ إخْواتِكُمْ" and "بَيْنَ أخْوَتِكُمْ". Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that religion unites them, and that they are brothers when they agree in their religion; so in agreeing in religion they returned to the root of lineage, because they are [descended] from Adam and Eve. Had their religions differed, they would have parted in lineage, even if originally they are from one father and one mother. Do you not see that the believing child does not inherit from the disbelieving father, nor does the believing close relative inherit from his disbelieving kinsman?

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِن قَوْمٍ﴾ — the verse: it may be that the one mocked is better than those who mock, and likewise it may be that the women who are mocked are better than the women who mock. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, forbade believing men to mock believing men, and believing women to mock believing women. ﴿وَلا تَلْمِزُوا أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾: "اَللَّمْزُ" and "اَلْهَمْزُ" are faulting and disparaging a person. Allah made known that their faulting one another clings to them: the fault of the one faulted clings to the one who faults. ﴿وَلا تَنابَزُوا بِالألْقابِ﴾: "اَلنَّبْزُ" and "اَللَّقَبُ" have one meaning: a Muslim should not call someone who was a Jew or a Christian and then accepted Islam by a nickname reproaching him for having been a Christian or a Jew. ﴿بِئْسَ الاسْمُ الفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الإيمانِ﴾, that is: evil is the name, that he should say to him: "يا يَهُودِيُّ" (O Jew) and "يا نَصْرانِيُّ" (O Christian), when he has believed. It may also apply to every nickname a person dislikes, because the believer ought to address his brother only by the names dearest to him.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِنَ الظَّنِّ إنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إثْمٌ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded avoiding much suspicion, namely that you think evil of people of goodness, when we know that what has appeared from him is good. As for people of evil and sinfulness, we may think of them the like of what has appeared from them.
His saying: ﴿وَلا يَغْتَبْ بَعْضُكم بَعْضًا﴾: "اَلْغَيْبَةُ" (backbiting) is (that a person is mentioned behind his back with evil, even if the evil is in him; as for mentioning him with what is not in him, that is "اَلْبَهْتُ" and "اَلْبُهْتانُ" (slander), (thus it has come from the Prophet ﷺ.
[Translator's note: the parentheses in the source are not closed.]
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أيُحِبُّ أحَدُكم أنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أخِيهِ مَيْتًا﴾ — "مَيِّتًا" is also permissible. Its interpretation is that your mentioning with evil someone who is not present with you is like eating his flesh while he is dead and does not feel it. Likewise you say of the backbiter: "فُلانٌ يَأْكُلُ لُحُومَ النّاسِ" (So-and-so eats people's flesh).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ﴾ — and it is read: "وَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ" — its interpretation is: "just as you hate to eat his flesh dead, likewise avoid mentioning him with evil in his absence."

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ إنّا خَلَقْناكم مِن ذَكَرٍ وأُنْثى﴾: We created you from Adam and Eve; all of you are children of one father and one mother, and to them you go back. ﴿وَجَعَلْناكم شُعُوبًا وقَبائِلَ لِتَعارَفُوا﴾: "اَلشَّعْبُ" (people, nation) is greater than the tribe. That is: He did not make you nations and tribes so that you might boast against one another; We made you so only that you might know one another. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known to them that the highest of them in rank with Him is the most God-fearing of them, and said: ﴿إنَّ أكْرَمَكم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أتْقاكُمْ﴾. Had it been read "أنَّ أكْرَمَكم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أتْقاكُمْ" (with fatḥa on the hamza), that would be permissible, in the sense of: "We made you nations so that you might know one another, because the noblest of you with Allah is the most God-fearing of you."

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قالَتِ الأعْرابُ آمَنّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا ولَكِنْ قُولُوا أسْلَمْنا ولَمّا يَدْخُلِ الإيمانُ في قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾: this is a place that people need to understand: where the believer (muʾmin) is distinguished from the Muslim, and where the two are equal. Islam is the outward display of submission and acceptance of what the Prophet ﷺ brought, and by that blood is protected. If, along with that outward display, there is conviction and affirmation by the heart, that is faith (īmān), and whoever is so described is a believer and a Muslim. He is the one who believes in Allah and His Messenger without doubt or uncertainty, who holds that performing the obligations is binding upon him and that striving with his person and his wealth is binding upon him, no doubt entering him in that: he is the believer, and he is the Muslim in truth, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتابُوا وجاهَدُوا بِأمْوالِهِمْ وأنْفُسِهِمْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الصّادِقُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 15], that is: when they say "we are believers", they are the truthful. As for one who outwardly displays acceptance of the Law and submits in order to ward off what is hateful, he is outwardly a Muslim while inwardly not affirming; that is the one who says "أسْلَمْتُ" (I have submitted), because faith requires that its possessor be one who affirms, since your saying "آمَنتُ بِكَذا وكَذا" (I believed in such-and-such) means "I affirmed it as true". So Allah excluded these people from faith and said: ﴿وَلَمّا يَدْخُلِ الإيمانُ في قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾, that is: you have not affirmed; you only submitted to seek refuge from being killed. So the believer conceals within him affirmation equal to what he displays; the Muslim complete in Islam is the one who displays obedience and in addition believes in it; and the Muslim who displayed Islam to seek refuge is not a believer in reality, except that his outward legal status is the status of the Muslims.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أنْ أسْلَمُوا قُلْ لا تَمُنُّوا عَلَيَّ إسْلامَكم بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكم أنْ هَداكم لِلإيمانِ إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾: it was said that this was revealed about the hypocrites: so know that if you are truthful, then you have submitted, and the favour upon you belongs to Allah, for His bringing you out of misguidance into guidance. It has also been said that it was revealed about others than the hypocrites, about some people among the Muslims who said: We believed, we emigrated, we did and we accomplished, and so they reminded the Messenger of Allah of that as a favour. The more likely — and Allah knows best — is that it concerns some people among the hypocrites.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنْ تُطِيعُوا اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ لا يَلِتْكم مِن أعْمالِكم شَيْئًا﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 14]: it is also read "لا يَأْلَتْكُمْ". Whoever reads "يَأْلَتْكُمْ", his proof is ﴿وَما ألَتْناهم مِن عَمَلِهِمْ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 21], whose meaning is "and We did not diminish them"; likewise "لا يَأْلَتْكُمْ": He will not diminish you. Whoever reads ﴿لا يَلِتْكُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 14], it is from "لاتَ، يَلِيتُ"; one says "لاتَهُ، يَلِيتُهُ" and "ألاتَهُ، يُلِيتُهُ" when one diminishes him as well. The meaning of the two is the same, I mean "يَأْلَتْكُمْ" and "يَلِتْكُمْ". The reading ﴿لا يَلِتْكُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 14] is more common, and the other — I mean "يَأْلَتْكُمْ" — is good and eloquent, and its proof in the Qur'an is as we have described.
